clue.text: Secret of behaving badly and escaping punishment

indicators.note: something behaving badly is out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A secret about someone's misbehaviour that they got away with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behaving badly' rearranges the eight letters of SECRET OF.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to go entirely unpunished, an idiom for escaping any penalty.

clue.text: Much less vicious, less hard individual

indicators.note: the second less tells us to take something away from the word before it

parts.note: something vicious can be lethal, deadly
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A comparison: something far less savage, a less tough person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much less' is the definition; the second 'less' is the deletion signal, so the clue uses the same word for two separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Let alone is an idiom used after a negative meaning still less or not to mention.

clue.text: See 1
It may help medicine go down, inserted into opening

definitions.text: It may help medicine go down, inserted into opening

indicators.note: inserted into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a loop is an opening, as in a loop of string

indicators.note: in a down entry, to go down is to read the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A sweet given to a child to make medicine palatable, popped into the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'go down' means read upwards. The whole clue also describes the sweet itself, popped into the mouth after a dose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet on a stick may be given to a child after nasty medicine and is put into the mouth.

clue.text: In a state of excitement as edges of dressing gown fall away

indicators.note: edges of points at the outer letters of the word that follows
fall away says those outer letters are dropped

parts.note: a bathrobe is a dressing gown

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited as the hem of their dressing gown drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges of ... fall away' strips B and E from BATHROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Athrob means throbbing or pulsating, as a heart does with excitement.

clue.text: Time to employ lifelong forte for dressing down

indicators.note: to employ letters is to put them to new use, so they are rearranged

parts.note: F is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud

explanation.surface: Using a lifelong strength to deliver a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employ' rearranges LIFELONG with F to make ELLINGOFF after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing down and a telling-off are both idioms for a reprimand or scolding.

clue.text: Foodstuff consumed in most of France at one time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Gaul was the ancient name for the region of France
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A food eaten across most of France in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final letter of the old name; 'in' puts the eaten piece inside, giving G-ATE-AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cake, a type of food.

clue.text: Perhaps banks lending capital make a killing

indicators.note: to bank is to border, so this word goes round the letter

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example

indicators.note: capital means the first, top letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Banks lending money to make huge profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' is a verb: SAY borders the L that 'capital' takes from 'lending'. 'make a killing' is profit in the surface but murder here.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill, so slaying is literally making a killing.

clue.text: Uncle Arthur protecting Frank

indicators.note: the words protecting the answer surround it, so it sits within them

explanation.surface: An uncle shielding a man named Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' says the letters sit inside UnCLE ARthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear can mean plain and open, as frank speech is.

clue.text: Pickled in ethanol without delay

indicators.note: pickled suggests the letters are drunk and muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something preserved in alcohol, or someone drunk on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickled' rearranges the letters of IN ETHANOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail is an idiom for paying immediately, promptly.

clue.text: Tour leader who sorts things out for the tourist

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ravel can mean to disentangle, so a raveller is one who sorts things out

explanation.surface: A tour guide who fixes problems for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel has two opposite senses, tangle and untangle; here it is the second, as Chambers allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone on a journey, a type of voyager.

clue.text: Suspicious of your slippery character, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: Wary of someone shifty, after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns YREEL round.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or distrustful, a synonym for suspicious.

clue.text: Slob in local knocked back bevvy

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
knocked back says the word is turned round

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's nearby pub
slob is an old word for mud or mire, as is ooze

explanation.surface: A lout in the pub downing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slob' is mud, not a person. 'knocked back' turns PUB into BUP, which holds OOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevvy is British slang for a drinking session, the same as a heavy drinking bout.

clue.text: Ed heard loud shouts

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Ed Balls is a British Labour politician

explanation.surface: Ed hears some noisy cries.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls, a well-known British Labour politician, supplies a surname that sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to shout or cry loudly, so the verb fits loud shouts.

clue.text: Lost nerve and skill

parts.note: ex means former, no longer had, as in something lost
pertness is cheekiness, nerve

explanation.surface: Losing one's nerve along with one's ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nerve' means cheek here, not courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertness is the quality of being expert, a synonym for skill.

clue.text: Spread Prohibition to Sleepy Hollow

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: hollow says the middle is emptied out

parts.note: a sleepy place is quiet

explanation.surface: Bringing Prohibition to the town of Sleepy Hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepy Hollow' looks like the American town; 'Hollow' removes the central I from QUIET.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is informal for a lavish meal laid out, like a feast.

clue.text: The noise of the bullring

indicators.note: the noise of says the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: The roar from a bullfighting arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullring' splits: 'bull' is Taurus, 'ring' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring-shaped solid, like a doughnut.

clue.text: Have young wife to provide assistance

parts.note: help means assistance

explanation.surface: A wife given help with a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth, used of dogs and other animals.

clue.text: Caress girl, hitting the mark precisely

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, short for Patricia
exactly right, as in off ... or a ... answer

explanation.surface: Stroking a girl, and doing it just right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for touching gently, a woman's name and an adjective for exactly apt.

clue.text: Fundamentalists preferring heartless sadism over British charm

indicators.note: preferring one thing over another means it is chosen in place of it
over completes the swap: one letter is chosen over another

parts.note: the Taliban are an Islamic fundamentalist movement

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: Extremists choosing cruelty over Britishness and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves SM from SADISM, which replaces the B in TALIBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck, an amulet or charm.

clue.text: Nod your heads off and hum

indicators.note: heads off says each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Nodding off while humming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' takes N and Y from NOD and YOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is British slang for a bad smell, which is a kind of scent.

clue.text: Master said individual spirit is to be stifled

indicators.note: stifled means smothered, held inside another word

parts.note: oral means spoken, said
I is a single one, an individual
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A teacher declares that personal spirit must be suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to be stifled' wraps the spoken word round the individual and the spirit. 'Master' is the original from which copies are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is the original work from which copies are made, as with a master recording.

clue.text: Frequently short of soft paper in gents

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so some letters are taken away

parts.note: oft is an old word for frequently
quires are sets of sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Often lacking soft toilet paper in the men's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' looks like the toilet but is the definition. 'short of' takes OFT from SOFT, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Squires are country gentlemen, so gents fits as a plural.

clue.text: Organs found in jumble sales

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit within the next words

explanation.surface: Body parts turning up at a charity sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to the letters inside jUMBLE Sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbles are the edible inner parts of a deer, offal organs.

clue.text: Twenty-four hours without a sound

indicators.note: without means the letters are removed

parts.note: Saturday is one twenty-four hour day
every letter a in the day is dropped

explanation.surface: A whole day passing in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Both As go from SATURDAY. 'sound' looks like noise but means solid and robust.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of strong and solid matches sturdy.

clue.text: Worst part about other papers for Guardian readers?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: lees are the dregs, the worst part
FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper other than the Guardian
I was a British newspaper, the i

explanation.surface: A rival press's take on the readership of the Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: The i and the Financial Times are newspapers other than the Guardian, whose readers are stereotyped as left-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lefties are left-wingers, the stereotypical readership of the Guardian newspaper.

clue.text: Brazilian footballer's extremely overrated as folk hero

parts.note: Robinho is a Brazilian footballer

indicators.note: extremely points at the outer letters, the extremes of the word

explanation.surface: A Brazilian player is wildly overrated as a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives O and D, the ends of 'overrated'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English outlaw of Sherwood is the archetypal folk hero.

clue.text: Artist starts to colour you blue

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A painter begins to tint you blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means risqué, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of risqué or saucy matches racy.

clue.text: Kind of plays on words without beginning to get tricky

indicators.note: without beginning says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: puns are plays on words
elfish means mischievous, tricky

explanation.surface: Wordplay that is no longer clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning' takes P from PUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unselfish is being generous and considerate, which is kind.

clue.text: Left order for portion of liver

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave a piece of liver.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is an honour in the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is divided into sections called lobes.

clue.text: See 26 across
It won't work in dry places, unfortunately

definitions.text: It won't work in dry places, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that fails in arid lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges DRY PLACES; a water clock needs water to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra is an ancient water clock, useless without water.

clue.text: Bash comic

explanation.surface: A party and a funny paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is slang for a celebration, and also a famous British children's comic title.
